title: Glagolitic and Cyrillic scripts (Cyril and Methodius)
summary: At the request of Prince Rastislav of Great Moravia, Emperor Michael III sent the Byzantine brothers Constantine (later Cyril) and Methodius there in 863. Cyril created the Glagolitic alphabet for Slavic, which had no written form, and they translated the liturgy, Gospels and Psalms and trained a Slavic-speaking clergy despite opposition from Latin clergy. The simpler Greek-based Cyrillic alphabet followed, made by Methodius or his disciple Clement of Ohrid; it underlies Russian, Bulgarian, Serbian and Macedonian writing.

uncertainty.note: Byzantine mission dispatched by Emperor Michael III at the request of Prince Rastislav of Great Moravia in 863 CE; Cyril created the Glagolitic script for this mission.
